title: docs(ci): pin four ci-cd-pipeline.md sections to what their jobs run
body:
Refs #8420 (the four measured defects)

⛔ Not `Fixes`: #8420 is a class card. The census in its classification comment accounted for all 36 workflow sections of `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`; this PR repairs and pins the **4** it measured as true defects. 13 sections that agree today are still held that way by nothing, and 11 legitimate exceptions are still unpinned — that work remains after this.

## What this changes

Four sections of `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` disagreed with what their workflow job actually runs. Each now names every first-party command its job runs, and each is pinned by a `commandParity` unit in `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`, following the shape the two units in `e09ae85f1` use.

| section | was missing | now named |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `## Performance Budget` | `pnpm check:sdui-registration-pins`, `pnpm check:eager-closure`, `turbo run build` | all three |
| `## Skill Examples` | `turbo run build` | named, with the empty-filter refusal that guards it |
| `### Changeset Release` | `pnpm build` | named, as the build both lanes' changesets steps run after |
| `### Spec Range Floors` | `turbo run build` | named, with its `!@object-ui/site` scope described |

Measured on the tree this branch was cut from, by the same helpers the pin uses, the before-state is exactly six readings — and it is the whole test's own output, not a description of it:

```
AssertionError: these jobs run commands that the section documenting them in content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md does not name:
  - performance-budget.yml `bundle-analysis`: pnpm check:eager-closure
  - performance-budget.yml `bundle-analysis`: pnpm check:sdui-registration-pins
  - performance-budget.yml `bundle-analysis`: turbo run build
  - skill-examples.yml `skill-examples`: turbo run build
  - changeset-release.yml `release`: pnpm build
  - spec-range-floors.yml `spec-range-floors`: turbo run build
```

## ⭐ The one reading that is not about naming a command

`## Performance Budget` stated, as its rule:

> Exactly one bundle-size number in this repository is enforced — this one:

and listed only the 350 KB entry-chunk line. The budget step opens `# TWO measurements, one verdict`. **A comment saying "verdict" is not evidence**, so the exit path was traced instead. It is, verbatim from the `Check console performance budget` step:

```bash
set +e
node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs
CLOSURE_CODE=$?
set -e

if [ "$CLOSURE_CODE" -eq 2 ]; then
  echo "budget_status=error" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "budget_message=… the eager-closure half of this gate returned no trustworthy VERDICT …" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$ENTRY_OVER" -eq 1 ] || [ "$CLOSURE_CODE" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "❌ BUDGET EXCEEDED"
  echo "budget_status=fail" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  exit 1
fi
```

⇒ **It enforces.** The closure gate's exit code is captured, and *both* of its non-zero values fail the step. The gate's own tail confirms the two codes are distinct verdicts rather than one:

```js
const statuses = [result.status, perChunk.status, sensitivity.status, freshness.status];
if (statuses.includes('error')) return 2;
return statuses.includes('fail') ? 1 : 0;
```

And the step is not advisory. Enumerating every `continue-on-error:` in `performance-budget.yml` beside the step that owns it — one command, so the zero for the budget step is a reading and not a failed grep:

```
- name: Setup Node.js                            ->  # `timeout-minutes` or `continue-on-error` to a generated post step.   (a comment)
- name: Build Console                            ->  # `continue-on-error` is deliberate and is NOT a fail-open: …          (a comment)
- name: Resolve the base-branch ceiling constants ->  continue-on-error: true
- name: Comment PR with results                  ->  continue-on-error: true
- name: Save Turbo Cache                         ->  continue-on-error: true
```

Three real ones, none on `Check console performance budget` and none on the job — the positive control for that zero being the three that the same command did find. `pnpm check:sdui-registration-pins` likewise carries none.

So the section now reads **"two measurements, either one can fail it"**, with both rows marked enforced. ⛔ **No ceiling value for the closure is written on the page** — objectui#8816 is an open decision on that exact ceiling and objectui#7848 measures its headroom. The page names the gate, says it enforces, and points at `pnpm check:eager-closure`, which prints payload, ceiling and headroom in one line. A test asserts the constant's value is absent from the page in all three of its spellings, reading the constant live from the gate so it tracks a re-baseline.

⚠️ Note for the next reader: `performance-budget.yml` contains a **comment** naming `pnpm check:eager-closure` inside the same `run:` block. That comment is not the evidence for anything here; the enforcement test explicitly filters comment lines out and requires exactly one real invocation.

## ⭐ The blind spot this set makes explicit

`commandParity` reads `run:` steps and nothing else. `changeset-release.yml` runs two first-party gates through `changesets/action@v1`'s `publish:` **input**, which a `run:`-only reader cannot see — so a naive extension reports the section as naming two commands its job "does not run". Deleting them would be the instrument editing the truth to match itself.

They are **declared** instead, with the reason, and the declaration is asserted as an exact set: a new phantom fails, and a declared one whose prose disappears fails as **stale**. The section also now says this out loud, so a later reader does not "fix" them out.

## ⚠️ One correction beyond naming a command, declared

While rewriting the sentence that quotes `pnpm changeset:publish`, its quoted body was found stale: the page said

> that script is `node scripts/check-published-dist-tooling.mjs && changeset publish`

while the root `package.json` has carried a middle leg for some time:

```
"changeset:publish": "node scripts/check-published-dist-tooling.mjs && node scripts/check-spec-range-floors.mjs && changeset publish"
```

The same section already said, three paragraphs later, that "`pnpm changeset:publish` runs both first on the publish lane anyway" — so the section contradicted itself. The quote is corrected; the third declared non-`run:` entry is that leg. This is the same defect class as the card's four (a section's command claims disagreeing with the truth), inside a sentence this PR was rewriting anyway, and it is now covered by the same exact-set assertion rather than left to review.

## Refactor, declared

The alias helpers (`aliasByScript` / `canonical` / `byGate`) and the `section()` reader move from inside the `vi-mock and shadcn` describe to module scope. **The rule is unchanged and its blast radius is unchanged** — `ci.yml`'s job table and the `lint.yml` section still call `commandParity` directly and are still pinned by the unmodified module-scope rule; only a describe that calls `byGate` opts in. The reason for the move is the card's own subject: two copies of a rule are two rules, and the next edit fixes one of them. The decision and its three stated limits stay documented where they landed.

## Verification

`pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` → **69 passed** (62 before this PR, 7 added).

Whole scripts suite, under the shared verification lock: `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__` → `Test Files 133 passed | 2 skipped (135)`, `Tests 3875 passed | 2 skipped (3877)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

Gates: `check:control-bytes` 0 · `check:doc-fences` 0 · `check:shell-escape-residue` 0 · `docs:check-links` 0 · `check:doc-types` 0 · `type-check:scripts` 0 · `lint:root` 0 errors (32 pre-existing warnings, none in the changed files).

`check:doc-snippets` returned **exit 2 — PRECONDITION NOT MET** ("the snippet program was NOT run: the packages it resolves against are not built"). That is not a verdict and is not reported as one. It is also not reachable by this diff: the diff adds **zero** fenced code blocks to the page, so the snippet program's input is unchanged. Left to CI, which builds first.

### Ablation — nine legs, each proved on disk and restored by blob hash

Every leg mutates the page, greps the marker on disk before and after (a mutation that changes no count aborts the run), asserts the mutated file's hash differs from the `HEAD` blob, runs the suite, restores with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH`, and then proves the restore two ways: the restored blob hash equals the `HEAD` blob and `git diff HEAD --name-only` is empty. A `trap … EXIT INT TERM` holds the restore on every exit path.

`HEAD` blob for the page: `aad790832184a3be0e69f9f99ff36a08de9cc6a7` — every leg's restored hash below is that value, and every leg's post-restore run is `69 passed`.

| # | leg | on-disk marker before → after | mutated exit | test that went red |
|:--|:--|:--:|:--:|:--|
| 1 | drop `pnpm check:sdui-registration-pins` from the prose | 1 → 0 | 1 | names every first-party command the four jobs actually run |
| 2 | drop both eager-closure spellings | 3 → 1 | 1 | same |
| 3 | drop `turbo run build` (Performance Budget) | 10 → 9 | 1 | same |
| 4 | drop `turbo run build` (Skill Examples) | 1 → 0 | 1 | same |
| 5 | drop `pnpm build` (Changeset Release) | 1 → 0 | 1 | same |
| 6 | drop `turbo run build` (Spec Range Floors) | 1 → 0 | 1 | same |
| 7 | ⭐ **phantom direction** — credit Spec Range Floors with `pnpm check:control-bytes`, which its job does not run | 1 → 2 | 1 | names no command outside the declared non-`run:` set |
| 8 | restore the retired *"Exactly one bundle-size number…"* sentence | 0 → 1 | 1 | says so on the page, with both rows marked enforced |
| 9 | restate the closure ceiling on the page | 0 → 1 | 1 | restates the closure ceiling nowhere on the page |

And the whole-page control, which is the one that answers *"was this pin green before the edit?"*: checking the page out at the branch point and running the suite gives **exit 1, 3 failed | 66 passed**, listing exactly the six readings quoted at the top. Restored hash `aad790832184a3be0e69f9f99ff36a08de9cc6a7`, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Changeset

`.changeset/8420-four-section-parity-pins.md`, empty frontmatter — documentation and test only, no package is released.

---

⛔ No `path:line` citation appears in this PR or in the page's new prose: `4e3a4f07e` measured 540 of 1267 such citations in this repository as already false. Everything above is cited by heading text or by content.
